objective: Expose request-bound VLM image encoding and generation timing, then test output-side latency ideas without weakening image detail or candidate review gates.

excluded: model prose outside the existing bounded debug trace

rejected_trials.name: label-keyed short wire schema
rejected_trials.reason: Only a sub-second observed gain, while one foreground robot was simultaneously marked as vehicle and ego and a meaningless 'none' open-set candidate was produced. The schema and normalization were removed.

rejected_trials.name: decoder max_consecutive_whitespaces=1 cold call
rejected_trials.reason: No output-token or character reduction; cold constrained-decoder setup was slower.

rejected_trials.name: decoder max_consecutive_whitespaces=1 warm call
rejected_trials.reason: Warm-cache call still emitted the same output size and was slower than the 31.723-second original-service baseline. The remote service was restored.

validation.extended_discovery_note: A broader 689-test discovery run exposed 19 failures outside the established gate, including Windows GBK/UTF-8 reads and legacy assertions. These were not counted as passing and were not used to accept this change.

boundaries: The accepted code adds request-bound observability only; it does not change inference semantics.
The timing values are repeated observations on one real image, not a latency distribution.
No image-token reduction was deployed because open-set and tiny-object recall have not been independently validated.
All generated annotations remain machine candidates, not human truth or training approval.
